title: Clinical features and prognostic factors in adults with bacterial meningitis (van de Beek et al., N Engl J Med 2004)

claims.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most common pathogen, accounting for 51% of episodes of community-acquired bacterial meningitis in adults.
claims.byte_quote: The most common pathogens were Streptococcus pneumoniae (51 percent of episodes) and Neisseria meningitidis (37 percent).

claims.text: Neisseria meningitidis was the second most common pathogen, accounting for 37% of episodes.
